summary: Research + 3 route-compared design directions for the Project Data page, scored into one spec

directions.name: Cost Ledger / Pareto
directions.thesis: A calm, single-column financial statement where the primary breakdown is a ranked horizontal-bar ledger sorted largest-first, so cost concentration reads in one glance like a printed estimate summary — restrained, dense, and authoritative.

sections.name: Statement header
sections.viz: Inline figure row inside one floating panel (12px radius, one soft shadow) — label/value pairs separated by hairline dividers, NOT a 3-up card grid. Carries the sheet selector + Category/Supplier/Space segmented control and one auto-insight sentence.
sections.whatItShows: The orientation line: which sheet, its total, sheet count, the single largest group, and a plain-language concentration insight.
sections.dataUsed: selectedEstimate.totalCost + currencyCode; summary.estimateSheets.length; topBucket (label+share); a new sentence from build-insight-sentence-style copy fed by the top 1-2 buckets' share.

sections.name: Cost ledger (PRIMARY)
sections.viz: Ranked horizontal-bar list, one dense row each: [color swatch 8px] [label, truncate] [proportional inline bar, fill width = share, track = surfaceMuted] [amount right-aligned tabular-nums] [share right-aligned]. Sorted largest-first, Other pinned last. Footer total row with a top hairline. Hover/focus highlights the row and (if shown) the secondary ring slice.
sections.whatItShows: Exactly where the selected sheet's money is concentrated, readable top-to-bottom as a Pareto — the bar replaces the donut as the primary mental model.
sections.dataUsed: buckets from collapseProjectChartBuckets(selectedSeries[groupingMode].allBuckets, 6): id, label, total, share, color (Okabe-Ito), rowCount for the Other count. Bar width = share; amounts via formatChartMoney; share via formatChartShare.

sections.name: Optional secondary ring
sections.viz: Tiny clean ring via CostDonutChart with hideCallouts (already crops to a ~190px square, no edge labels). Collapsed behind a quiet 'Show ring' disclosure or shown only at xl in a narrow right rail; labels live entirely in the ledger.
sections.whatItShows: A part-to-whole glance for people who think in pie shape, without ever owning the labels.
sections.dataUsed: Same buckets array + total; hideCallouts=true so the unreadable 720x560 edge callouts never render.

sections.name: Cost composition
sections.viz: A single thin 100%-width stacked composition strip (one bar, 3 segments) + an inline figure line beneath it. Uses three restrained tints, not full categorical hues, to avoid competing with the ledger.
sections.whatItShows: NEW: how the sheet total splits into direct cost vs miscellaneous vs contingency — a contractor-relevant fact never shown today.
sections.dataUsed: Per-row facts: direct = qty*unitCost summed; misc = miscCost summed; contingency = (qty*unitCost)*contingencyPercentage/100 summed. Requires a new server-side aggregate (see risks).

sections.name: Cost across sheets
sections.viz: Kept largely as-is: ranked stacked horizontal bars (already on-brand for this direction) + the full data table and legend below. Reordered to sit after the single-sheet ledger so the page reads single-sheet -> cross-sheet.
sections.whatItShows: How sheets compare in total and cost mix without implying a timeline.
sections.dataUsed: summary.rollup, seriesByEstimateId per sheet, top-4 segments + Other (existing buildStackedRows / buildTotalsOnlyRows).

dataSurfaced: Direct cost vs miscellaneous vs contingency composition of the sheet total (computable from row facts qty*unitCost / miscCost / contingencyPercentage, never surfaced today)
Pareto cumulative reading: the ranked bars make 'top 2 groups = 61%' legible at a glance, plus an explicit total footer row that the donut never showed
Per-group row counts surfaced as the 'Other (n)' count and available as a quiet secondary metric per ledger row
directions.mobileBehavior: Already single-column friendly. Statement header figures wrap to stacked label/value pairs (no card grid to collapse). The ledger row keeps swatch + label + amount + share on the first line and drops the inline proportional bar to a thin full-width bar on a second line beneath the label, so nothing is squeezed below ~3px. The optional ring stays collapsed on mobile. Cost-composition strip stays full width (it already is). Cost-across-sheets table gets horizontal scroll as today.
risks: Cost composition (direct/misc/contingency) is NOT pre-aggregated: ProjectChartBucket only carries `total`, and the repo ships KB of buckets not raw rows for data-minimization (SEC-1). Surfacing it needs a new server-side aggregate in project-charts-repository / aggregate-project-charts, not a client compute — otherwise drop this section for v1.

The ledger bar + the BreakdownTable are now near-duplicates; must merge them into ONE component (the ledger IS the table) or the page regains redundancy — the same redundancy that made the donut callouts pointless.

Composition strip tints must stay OUTSIDE the Okabe-Ito chart palette rule yet still read as data; risk of either violating the palette exception or producing low-contrast greys that fail AA. Use distinct AA-safe neutrals/inks, validated.
Proportional inline bars share the row width with right-aligned amount+share; long PHP figures + long labels can collide on narrow desktop columns — needs min-widths and truncation, tested at ~380px.
Keeping the secondary ring at all risks reintroducing a second labels surface; it must be strictly label-free (hideCallouts) and visually subordinate, or cut entirely.
directions.whyStrong: This is the most conservative and most on-brand of the directions: a ranked bar ledger is literally how contractors read an estimate summary, so it lowers cognitive load instead of decorating. It eliminates the headline callout bug structurally — the donut is demoted to an optional label-free ring (hideCallouts), so the unreadable 5-6px edge text simply never renders, and the labels live where they're already legible. It reuses the existing buckets/color/format pipeline almost untouched (low blast radius), collapses to mobile naturally because it's already one column, and earns its keep by surfacing one genuinely new contractor-relevant fact (direct/misc/contingency composition). It shouts nothing, decorates nothing, and the tool disappears behind the numbers.

directions.name: Cost Anatomy
directions.thesis: A composition-first ledger: a calm grey canvas where one quiet full-width DIRECT / MISC / CONTINGENCY strip names how the money is built, then a single dense breakdown matrix dissects it by category, supplier, or space — precise, architectural, no donut and no hero metrics.

sections.name: Sheet selector + anatomy header
sections.viz: Plain in-app dropdown (existing DropdownSelect, boxed) in the page chrome row; one small label-style total beneath the panel title — NOT an oversized hero numeral
sections.whatItShows: Which sheet is in focus and its single total cost, row count, and name as quiet meta
sections.dataUsed: selectedEstimate.totalCost, selectedEstimate.rowCount, name, currencyCode from ProjectDataEstimateSheet; estimateSheets list for the dropdown

sections.name: Cost anatomy strip (the lead)
sections.viz: One full-width 100%-stacked horizontal composition strip, ~28px tall, rounded-xs, three segments DIRECT / MISC / CONTINGENCY, with three inline legend ticks (color swatch + label + amount + share) below it — no axis, no gridlines
sections.whatItShows: How the selected sheet's money is composed before any category cut: direct line-item cost vs miscellaneous add-ons vs contingency reserve
sections.dataUsed: NEW per-sheet composition aggregate: DIRECT = sum(qty*unitCost), MISC = sum(miscCost), CONTINGENCY = sum(subtotal*contingencyPercentage/100), derived from the same row facts calculateProjectChartRowTotal already uses but NOT currently shipped — must be added to the series payload server-side

sections.name: Contingency/misc insight line
sections.viz: One calm secondary-ink sentence directly under the strip (reuses the build-insight-sentence.ts tone, new composition template)
sections.whatItShows: Surfaces contingency exposure and misc as first-class risk: e.g. 'Contingency adds ₱176k (8%) on top of direct cost; misc is ₱121k (6%).'
sections.dataUsed: Same composition aggregate (direct/misc/contingency totals + shares); a small new composition-sentence builder modeled on build-insight-sentence

sections.name: Breakdown matrix (category / supplier / space)
sections.viz: Ranked horizontal-bar matrix — one row per bucket: color swatch + label, an inline proportional bar (share of sheet), right-aligned amount, share %, and row count. Replaces the donut+table 2-col grid entirely. Space mode renders the existing indented hierarchical tableRows tree using the same row grammar (depth indent, group rollup non-colored, area leaves colored)
sections.whatItShows: Where the (mostly direct) cost concentrates, cut by category, supplier, or space; bar length and color cross-reference each bucket without a separate chart
sections.dataUsed: buckets (collapseProjectChartBuckets, top 6 + Other) for category/supplier; seriesByEstimateId[id].space tableRows for the Space tree; bucket-color.ts Okabe-Ito hues for marks only; format.ts for money/share

sections.name: Across sheets anatomy
sections.viz: One composition strip per sheet (same DIRECT/MISC/CONTINGENCY grammar as Panel 1), stacked vertically, each with its total and a right-aligned contingency-exposure % column; falls back to totals-only single-segment bars at >20 sheets, mixed-currency banner unchanged
sections.whatItShows: Compares not just sheet totals but each sheet's cost anatomy and contingency exposure side by side — making an over-reserved or misc-heavy sheet visible at a glance
sections.dataUsed: Per-sheet composition aggregate for every loaded sheet + estimateSheets totals; reuses existing rollup.kind mixed/single guard and costAcrossSheetsMode totals-only switch

dataSurfaced: DIRECT vs MISC vs CONTINGENCY composition per sheet (currently computed in the total but never shown as parts)
Contingency exposure as an explicit share and amount, framed as first-class risk
Misc cost as an explicit share and amount rather than being silently folded into the total
Per-bucket row count alongside amount and share (already in ProjectChartBucket.rowCount but unused in the current table)
Cross-sheet contingency-exposure comparison (which sheet reserves more, proportionally)
directions.mobileBehavior: Single column. Anatomy strip stays full-width and readable (segments keep min-width; tiny segments collapse their inline amount but keep the swatch+share in a wrapped legend list below). Breakdown matrix drops the inline bar on the narrowest widths and keeps label + amount + share + count as a dense list, or keeps a thin bar above each label; segmented Category/Supplier/Space control becomes full-width. Across-sheets strips stack with total beneath each label. No horizontal scroll except the optional raw data table which scrolls inside its panel.
risks: The lead viz depends on a composition aggregate (direct/misc/contingency) that is NOT currently shipped to the client — the wire only carries pre-bucketed category/supplier/space series plus a single totalCost. This requires a new server-side aggregate in project-charts-repository/aggregate-project-charts and a payload type change; without it Panel 1 cannot render. This is the single biggest build cost of Direction B.

Adding raw direct/misc/contingency sums to the wire must respect the existing data-minimization stance (SEC-1: qty/unitCost never cross the wire) — ship only the three aggregated sums per sheet, never the row facts.

Three segments only (direct/misc/contingency) means the strip carries little visual variety; if misc and contingency are near-zero on many real sheets the lead viz can look like a near-solid bar — the insight line must carry the weight in that common case.

Okabe-Ito palette is categorical, not semantic; direct/misc/contingency should use a restrained 3-step sequence (e.g. ink + two greys, or three palette hues) chosen to avoid implying misc/contingency are 'categories' — needs a deliberate small palette decision since these are NOT bucket ids.
Replacing the donut removes a chart some users may expect; mitigated because the ranked-bar matrix is strictly more readable and the screenshot proves the donut callouts are already unreadable.
Space-mode hierarchical tree in a ranked-bar matrix needs careful indent + rollup styling so group totals don't double-count visually against their area leaves.
directions.whyStrong: It directly answers the owner's actual ask ('analyze the cost data') by exposing the one thing the current page hides — how the money is composed (direct/misc/contingency) and how much contingency risk is baked in — rather than re-skinning a donut. It kills the headline unreadable-callout bug definitionally by removing the donut and using full-width bars whose length IS the data, with every label/amount/share/count inline so there is nothing to crop or scale-shrink. It is the boldest in data-richness while staying inside the brand: calm grey canvas, white panels with one shadow, 12px-max type, 3px/12px radii, Okabe-Ito only on marks, secondary #5D5D5D for load-bearing meta. It also revives the unused build-insight-sentence pattern as a quiet one-line takeaway, so the tool states the finding without shouting.

directions.name: Direction C — Insight-led / analyst Data page
directions.thesis: A quiet analyst's worksheet: a plain-language insight line and the two numbers that matter lead, then a single ranked-bar ledger you read top-to-bottom and drill in place — calm, dense, action-first, no decorative donut.

sections.name: Insight header (Panel A)
sections.viz: Auto-generated plain-language sentence (≤12px ink) + an inline 3-up numeral strip (sheet total / top-group share / groups-carrying-80%); sheet dropdown + Category|Supplier|Space segmented control on the same row
sections.whatItShows: The one thing to act on first: which group dominates, how concentrated the sheet is, and how few groups carry the bulk — so the estimator instantly sees the biggest lever and single-group risk
sections.dataUsed: buckets[0] + buckets[1] (label/total/share) from seriesByEstimateId[sheet][mode].allBuckets; selectedEstimate.totalCost; an 80%-cumulative-share count computed client-side from the ranked buckets. Sentence built by a new buildConcentrationSentence() reusing build-insight-sentence.ts tone (driverClause/formatDeltaPercent style)

sections.name: Where the cost is — ranked ledger (Panel B)
sections.viz: Ranked horizontal bars, one row per bucket, sorted desc: [color tick][label][proportional bar track][amount][share][rowCount ▸]. A thin cumulative '80%' divider rule sits between the rows that cross 80%. Replaces the donut+table 2-col entirely
sections.whatItShows: The full breakdown as a single scannable lever list — longest bar = biggest lever; the 80% rule shows how much of the sheet a contractor must control to control most of the cost
sections.dataUsed: collapseProjectChartBuckets(...allBuckets, 6) for total/share/rowCount/color; bar width = total/maxTotal. Cumulative-share threshold computed inline

sections.name: Drill-in sub-ledger (Panel B, expanded)
sections.viz: Clicking a row expands an inline indented sub-ledger of the same ranked-bar style (depth-aware), pushing rows below it down — never a modal, never a second chart
sections.whatItShows: Why a group is big: in Space mode, the real group/area/Own-items tree; in Category/Supplier mode, the next level (spaces or suppliers contributing to that group) so the estimator finds the exact line cluster to attack
sections.dataUsed: Space mode: existing hierarchical tableRows tree (kind group/area, depth) from buildSpaceTableRows. Category/Supplier: a small server addition exposing per-bucket child buckets (cross-tab by space/supplier) — or, MVP fallback, link the row to the estimate's filtered line-item table

sections.name: Cost composition strip (Panel C)
sections.viz: A single full-width 100% horizontal composition strip: Direct cost / Misc / Contingency, three segments, neutral-to-accent, with inline % labels
sections.whatItShows: Surfaces never-shown data: how much of the total is real direct cost vs misc add-ons vs contingency padding — a fast sanity/markup check
sections.dataUsed: NEW server aggregation: sum(qty*unitCost)=direct, sum(miscCost)=misc, sum(subtotal*contingency%/100)=contingency per sheet, derived from the same row facts calculateProjectChartRowTotal already reads. Added to the pre-aggregated series so raw facts stay off the wire

sections.name: Across sheets (Panel D)
sections.viz: An insight sentence (real buildInsightSentence output) + ranked total bars per sheet, with the per-sheet segmented-mix stacked bar and full data table moved behind a single '▸ Show per-sheet mix' disclosure
sections.whatItShows: Which sheet is biggest and by how much, in words, then the ranked totals; deeper mix comparison is available but not forced on first read
sections.dataUsed: summary.estimateSheets totals for ranked bars; existing buildStackedRows/legend/table for the disclosure; buildInsightSentence fed the top two sheets as baseline/comparand

dataSurfaced: Direct cost vs misc vs contingency composition (Panel C) — currently computable from row facts but never displayed
Concentration metric: how many groups carry 80% of the sheet (single-group / few-group risk signal)
Per-row line-item count (rowCount) promoted to a visible drill affordance on every ranked row
Plain-language 'biggest lever' identification instead of leaving the estimator to read it off a donut
Cumulative-share 80% threshold rule rendered directly on the ranked ledger
directions.mobileBehavior: Single column throughout. Panel A: sentence wraps full-width; the 3 numerals stack to a 1-col list (label above value). Sheet dropdown + grouping control stack and go full-width (grouping control becomes a full-width segmented row). Panel B ranked rows keep [tick+label] on line 1 and [bar] full-width on line 2 with [amount · share · ▸count] right-aligned beneath — bar always has room, never the donut's scaled-text failure. Drill expands inline as before. Panel C composition strip stays full-width (it is already a horizontal strip). Panel D ranked total bars stack; the mix disclosure table scrolls horizontally inside its panel (overflow-x-auto) exactly like the existing table.
risks: Category/Supplier drill needs a server-side per-bucket child aggregation that doesn't exist yet; without it those modes either fall back to a line-item-table link or ship drill for Space only (Space already has the tree) — scope creep risk

Composition strip (Panel C) requires adding direct/misc/contingency sums to the pre-aggregated series; must stay server-side to preserve the data-minimization guarantee (raw qty/unitCost must not cross the wire)
Removing the donut is a visible identity change — owner may still want a small ring somewhere; mitigate by keeping CostDonutChart available but not leading with it
build-insight-sentence.ts is comparison-shaped (baseline vs comparand); the single-sheet concentration headline needs a new sibling generator, not a direct reuse, or the sentence will read awkwardly
An auto-sentence that is wrong/over-confident on edge data (one bucket, equal buckets, zero total) erodes trust — needs the same equal/new/empty cases the existing generator already handles
Ranked bars + 80% rule can feel busy if every row also shows a bar track, amount, share, and count; must enforce restraint (one accent, secondary meta, no second color in chrome)
directions.whyStrong: It is the most 'work on this' direction: it answers the estimator's actual question — where is the biggest lever and where is the single-group risk — in one sentence and one scannable list, instead of making them decode a donut. It deletes the headline callout bug at the root by removing the donut as the lead, replacing it with ranked bars that are readable at any width and degrade cleanly to mobile. It honors every brand constraint (12px max type, 3/8/12px radii, neutral ink/secondary meta, Okabe-Ito only on the bar marks and never in chrome, one soft shadow on white panels, calm grey canvas) while staying dense and understated. And it earns its keep by surfacing genuinely new, computable-but-hidden data (direct/misc/contingency composition, 80% concentration) rather than redecorating what was already shown.

opportunities.title: Concentration / top-N dominance callout (HHI-lite)
opportunities.whatItShows: A single understated sentence + the donut: how concentrated this sheet's cost is — e.g. 'Top 3 categories carry 78% of this sheet' or 'Casework alone is 31% of the total.' Surfaces whether cost is spread or load-bearing on one bucket.
opportunities.computation: From the already-sorted allBuckets: cumulativeShare of top 1/2/3 buckets = sum(buckets[0..n].share); dominant = buckets[0].share. Optionally a Herfindahl index = sum(share_i^2) for a single 0-1 'concentration' scalar. All pure client math on shipped {share,total}.
opportunities.dataSource: 100% client-side from existing seriesByEstimateId[id][mode].allBuckets. Nothing new from server. topBucket is already computed in ProjectDataClient.
opportunities.notes: Highest value-to-effort. Directly answers the 'analyze the cost data' ask, reuses build-insight-sentence.ts style, needs zero payload change, and gives the page a real headline instead of redundant donut+table. Replaces the weak 'Largest group' KPI.

opportunities.title: Cross-sheet variance insight sentence (baseline vs comparand) — activate the dormant engine
opportunities.whatItShows: The one human sentence the comparison engine was built for: 'Ground Floor is ₱2.5M (−53%) lower than General Requirements, driven mostly by Floor Finishes (−₱1.8M) and Furniture (−₱0.2M).' Turns the mute stacked-bar section into an explained variance.
opportunities.computation: buildProjectChartComparisonView({estimates, seriesByEstimateId, groupingMode, estimateIds:[a,b]}) then buildInsightSentence(view.insight). Both functions already exist and are pure; they consume exactly the shipped series map.
opportunities.dataSource: Client-side. Requires the page to load series for the compared pair (2 sheets) into seriesByEstimateId, not just the single selected sheet. Repository ALREADY supports this (getProjectChartsData selectedEstimateIds slices up to 3); project-data-repository currently passes only [selected]. So: a 1-line repo wiring change to request the pair, NOT a payload-shape change.
opportunities.notes: The build-insight-sentence.ts generator and the whole project-comparison-view view-model are fully built, tested, and UNUSED on this page. This is the single biggest latent value. No new columns cross the wire; only which estimate ids get aggregated. SEC-1 unaffected (still pre-bucketed).

opportunities.title: Per-bucket delta table across sheets (variance, not just totals)
opportunities.whatItShows: For the across-sheets table, add Δ and Δ% columns vs a chosen baseline sheet per category/supplier/space bucket, sorted by |Δ| — the 'what moved and by how much' view. The biggest movers, biggest first.
opportunities.computation: view.buckets each carry baselineTotal, comparandTotal, delta, deltaPercent, already computed by buildProjectChartComparisonView. Render delta with sign + colorless ink (no green/red decoration beyond a restrained accent).
opportunities.dataSource: Client-side from the same pre-bucketed series map (needs the compared sheets loaded, same wiring as opportunity 2). No raw facts.
opportunities.notes: Reuses ProjectChartComparisonViewBucket end-to-end. Pairs naturally with the insight sentence. Cap to top movers to stay calm/dense, not a wall of rows.

opportunities.title: Average cost per line item, per bucket
opportunities.whatItShows: A 4th table column: avg ₱/line = bucket.total / bucket.rowCount, plus line count. Distinguishes 'expensive because many cheap lines' (e.g. fixtures) from 'expensive because few big-ticket lines' (e.g. casework). A real estimator signal.
opportunities.computation: bucket.total / bucket.rowCount, guarding rowCount===0. Pure client.
opportunities.dataSource: Client-side. rowCount is ALREADY on every ProjectChartBucket in the shipped payload — confirmed in types.ts and aggregate-project-charts toBucket. Nothing new from server.
opportunities.notes: Free given rowCount already ships. Low-decoration, high-density add that fits the 'precise/architectural' brand. Useful as a sortable column rather than a hero.

opportunities.title: Cost composition: direct vs misc vs contingency split
opportunities.whatItShows: How the sheet total decomposes into direct cost (qty*unitCost), miscellaneous cost, and contingency — e.g. 'Direct ₱1.9M / Misc ₱120k / Contingency ₱180k (9%).' Answers 'how much of my number is real work vs padding' which the current page cannot.
opportunities.computation: Per row: direct=qty*unitCost; misc=miscCost; contingency=direct*contingencyPercentage/100. Sum across the sheet (and optionally per bucket). The per-row math ALREADY exists in calculateProjectChartRowTotal — it computes these three terms and then throws away the split, keeping only the sum.
opportunities.dataSource: SERVER CHANGE REQUIRED. The split is computed server-side but collapsed before shipping; only bucket.total crosses the wire. ProjectChartModeSeries/ProjectChartBucket would need to also carry {directTotal, miscTotal, contingencyTotal} (a few pre-aggregated scalars — still bucketed, still SEC-1-compliant since no per-row qty/unitCost is exposed). project-charts-repository + project-comparison-view buildEstimateSeries + types.ts all need the new fields.
opportunities.notes: FLAGGED: requires extending the server payload contract (new aggregated scalars on the series/bucket). It does NOT violate SEC-1 — it ships sums, not raw qty/unitCost — but it deliberately widens the deliberately-minimal contract, so it's an owner decision. High estimator value; the only insight here that genuinely needs new server data.

opportunities.title: Hierarchical space breakdown (tree), not a flat donut
opportunities.whatItShows: In Space mode, an indented tree (Floor 1 > Living Room > items) with rollup subtotals and shares, instead of the flat top-6 donut buckets. Shows where in the building the money sits.
opportunities.computation: buildSpaceTableRows already produces ProjectChartTableRow[] with depth/kind(group|area)/rollup totals/shares — fully built and test-pinned in aggregate-project-charts.ts.
opportunities.dataSource: SERVER CHANGE REQUIRED. The tree (tableRows) is built on the server but is part of the fat ProjectChartSeries, NOT the slim ProjectChartModeSeries that actually ships (which keeps only {total, allBuckets}). To render the tree the payload must also carry tableRows for space mode.
opportunities.notes: FLAGGED: payload extension (add tableRows to space-mode series). The computation is done and tested; only the wire contract drops it. Bounded size (one tree per loaded sheet). Lower priority than the composition split unless space is a primary lens for the owner.

opportunities.title: Supplier exposure / dependency callout
opportunities.whatItShows: In Supplier mode: concentration on a single vendor — 'One supplier covers 41% of this sheet' or 'No-supplier lines = 22% (₱x unassigned).' A procurement-risk read.
opportunities.computation: Same concentration math as opportunity 1 but applied to supplier-mode allBuckets; the 'No supplier' bucket is already a real bucket id from resolveSupplierBucket. share/total already shipped.
opportunities.dataSource: Client-side from existing supplier-mode series. No server change.
opportunities.notes: Reuses the concentration primitive with a procurement framing. The 'No supplier' / unassigned share doubles as a data-quality nudge. Keep it as one understated line, not a separate card.

opportunities.title: Data-quality / coverage strip (uncategorized, no-supplier, unassigned-space, truncation)
opportunities.whatItShows: A quiet footnote: '8% Uncategorized, 22% No supplier, 5% Unassigned space — totals from a capped read' so the user trusts (or distrusts) the breakdown.
opportunities.computation: Share of the 'uncategorized'/'No supplier'/'unassigned-space'/'Other' buckets (stable ids from the resolvers) + existing didTruncate flag. Pure client.
opportunities.dataSource: Client-side; bucket ids and didTruncate already in payload (didTruncate already surfaced as a Banner).
opportunities.notes: Low glamour but builds trust in every other number and fits 'understated.' Folds the existing truncation banner into a single coverage line instead of a separate alarm.

payloadGaps: Per-row cost composition split is computed then discarded: calculateProjectChartRowTotal derives direct (qty*unitCost), misc (miscCost), and contingency (direct*contingencyPercentage/100) per row, but each bucket ships only the summed `total`. To show direct/misc/contingency the series/bucket must carry pre-aggregated {directTotal, miscTotal, contingencyTotal} scalars (still bucketed — SEC-1 safe, no raw qty/unitCost on the wire).

Space-mode hierarchy is dropped on the wire: aggregate-project-charts builds a full ProjectChartTableRow[] tree (buildSpaceTableRows, depth/kind/rollups, test-pinned), but the shipped ProjectChartModeSeries keeps only {total, allBuckets}. The slim payload (project-comparison-view buildEstimateSeries) discards tableRows, so the page can only render a flat donut for spaces.

Single-sheet load on the Data route: project-data-repository requests series for only the selected estimate (selectedEstimateIds:[selected]). The comparison engine (delta/insight) needs >=2 sheets' series. The repository already supports loading up to 3 (getProjectChartsData/SELECTED_ESTIMATE_LOAD_LIMIT) — this is a wiring gap, not a contract gap; no new field types needed.

No precomputed insight/variance on the wire: the comparison view-model (buildProjectChartComparisonView) and the insight-sentence generator (build-insight-sentence.ts) are pure client functions that already consume the shipped series map, but neither is invoked on this page. The 'analysis' the prompt asks for is mostly latent code, not missing data — provided the compared pair's series are loaded.

Raw per-row facts (qty, unitCost, supplierId, contingencyPercentage) are intentionally server-only per SEC-1 data-minimization. Any insight needing per-line distributions (e.g. histogram of line costs, true big-ticket outliers, supplier price variance) is NOT feasible without either pre-aggregating new summary stats server-side or relaxing SEC-1 — flag to owner; do not ship raw facts.

findings.point: Cleveland-McGill hierarchy places angle/area at rank 3-4, position at rank 1 — the foundational argument against pie/donut for comparison tasks
findings.evidence: Cleveland & McGill (1984) ranked elementary perceptual tasks: position along a common scale (most accurate) > length/direction/angle > area > volume/curvature > shading. Pie and donut charts require viewers to judge angle and area; bar charts use position and length. The 1984 position-angle experiment directly pitted pie vs bar, and bar outperformed. Their conclusion: pie/donut 'need to be constructed with very careful consideration or give way to chart types with a better-prioritised order.' Source confirmed via multiple independent secondary analyses.

findings.point: For cost breakdown with ranking intent, a sorted horizontal bar chart is the correct default — it encodes both magnitude and rank simultaneously on a single positional axis
findings.evidence: Consensus across Ataccama, Domo, and Luzmo sources: bar charts are superior when the primary goal is comparison or when there are more than 4-5 categories. Sorted horizontal bars allow long category labels (CSI divisions, trade names, phase names) to read naturally. A stacked horizontal bar works for a single-row total-with-composition view, but individual segment comparison degrades past 4 segments. Ranked bar is the go-to for estimating tools because it surfaces the dominant cost driver at a glance, which is the actionable signal in professional estimating.

findings.point: Donut earns its place in exactly one professional-tool scenario: a single-metric progress/completion ring with a center callout, not for multi-segment cost composition
findings.evidence: Domo, Toucan Toco, and the Logi Analytics KPI pattern all describe the same legitimate use: a 2-segment donut (filled vs. remainder) with a large center number — budget consumed vs. total, percent complete, etc. This works because the viewer reads the center number directly; the ring is just a progress affordance, not a precision comparison. As soon as there are 3+ segments, the angle-perception problem re-emerges. Stephen Few's 'Save the Pies for Dessert' (cited in Ataccama) draws this same boundary. The donut as a KPI ring in a dense professional tool is justified; the donut as a 7-segment cost-breakdown chart is not.

findings.point: Professional finance and estimating tools converge on: waterfall for incremental buildup, stacked bar for multi-period composition, ranked bar for single-period breakdown — pie/donut rarely appear in analyst-facing UX
findings.evidence: Finance Alliance's survey of professional financial charts describes the selection pattern explicitly: simple proportions → pie or stacked bar; incremental buildup (net income changes, change orders stacking to total) → waterfall; multi-period comparisons → grouped bar. Estimating software reviews (Sage, ProEst, Archdesk) describe 'detailed cost breakdowns' and 'professional reporting templates' but the dominant output format is tabular + bar, not pie. Waterfall charts are particularly common in change-order and budget-vs-actual contexts, which is structurally similar to construction cost assembly.

findings.point: Stacked bar past 4 segments loses readability; the fix is not a donut, it is an 'Other' rollup plus a drill-down pattern
findings.evidence: Domo and CleanChart both document the 3-4 segment ceiling for stacked bars: beyond that, smallest segments become unreadable and composition comparison across bars fails. The professional convention is to group tail items into 'Other' and expose a drill-down or secondary breakdown table. This is how Bloomberg, Sage, and cost-management SaaS (CloudZero, Finout) handle long cost hierarchies — a top-level bar with an 'Other' bucket, plus a subordinate detail view, never a 14-segment pie.

findings.point: WCAG AA requires: 4.5:1 contrast for text labels; 3:1 (SC 1.4.11) for non-text chart elements (bars, fills); color must never be the sole differentiator (SC 1.4.1); every chart needs a structured text alternative (SC 1.1.1)
findings.evidence: DubBot's 2024 accessible charts guide enumerates: SC 1.1.1 (text alternative, not just chart type description — must convey the actual data), SC 1.4.1 (color alone cannot convey meaning — use pattern fills or direct labels), SC 1.4.3 (4.5:1 for text including data labels and axis labels), SC 1.4.11 (3:1 for adjacent colored chart elements — white dividers between segments are the standard fix). 8% of men have color vision deficiency; red/green pairs are the highest-risk combination in cost/budget UIs (positive/negative, on-budget/over-budget).

findings.point: Direct labeling on bars eliminates the legend-lookup cost that makes dense tools unusable; this also resolves the color-alone WCAG problem
findings.evidence: Ataccama and Eval Academy both note that pie/donut charts force legend lookups or callout labels, adding cognitive context-switching. Horizontal bar charts with direct end-of-bar labels (or inline labels for stacked bars with sufficient segment width) remove the legend entirely. For a professional estimating tool, this is a double win: faster scan for the user and accessible-by-default (the text label is the differentiator, not the color).

findings.point: The only documented case where a donut still earns its place in a pro estimating context is a single 'budget consumed' ring on a project summary card — when the number in the center IS the content and the ring is merely a progress affordance
findings.evidence: Logi Analytics KPI donut pattern, VizWiz Tableau tip, and Toucan Toco all describe this identically: one filled segment + one empty segment, large center metric. The ring's job is spatial emphasis on a number the user already reads directly. This is structurally different from a breakdown chart. In an estimating tool, this could appear on a project card showing '73% of budget consumed' — but the cost breakdown behind that number should be a sorted horizontal bar in the detail view.

priorArt.donutVsBarVerdict: Horizontal ranked bar wins for cost breakdown in professional estimating tools. The research case is settled (Cleveland-McGill 1984, confirmed by Ataccama/Domo/peer lit): angle and area encoding (donut/pie) are rank 3-4 in human perceptual accuracy; position along a common scale (bar) is rank 1. For a cost-breakdown view with 4+ categories, a sorted horizontal bar surfacing the dominant cost driver is correct. A donut earns its place only as a single-metric progress ring (e.g., '73% of budget consumed') with a large center callout — that is, when the user reads the center number and the ring is a spatial emphasis aid, not a precision comparison. Never use a multi-segment donut for cost breakdown in a dense professional tool.
recommendations: Use a sorted horizontal bar chart as the primary cost breakdown visualization. Sort descending by value so the dominant cost driver is always first. Direct-label bar ends with the formatted value and percentage — this eliminates legend lookup and satisfies WCAG SC 1.4.1 (color not sole differentiator).

Cap visible segments at 5-6 in any stacked or multi-series view; roll tail items into an 'Other' bucket with a drill-down affordance. Beyond that threshold, segment comparison accuracy degrades regardless of chart type.

Reserve the donut for a single-metric KPI ring (one fill + one remainder, large center number) on project summary cards or header KPIs — not for composition breakdowns. If you use it, ensure the center callout is the primary readable element and the ring is secondary.

Use waterfall charts when showing how individual cost items build to a total (e.g., base cost + labor + markup + contingency = contract value). This is the correct chart type for incremental-buildup narratives common in estimating.

For WCAG AA compliance: maintain 4.5:1 contrast on all data labels and axis labels; 3:1 on adjacent colored bar fills (SC 1.4.11); use white dividers between adjacent colored segments; never use red/green as the only differentiator for positive/negative values (use text labels or shape redundancy). Provide a structured data table or aria-described-by for every chart.

Avoid 100% stacked horizontal bars for cross-project comparison — only the leftmost segment reads accurately; all others require the viewer to estimate a floating baseline, which is rank 2 in the Cleveland-McGill hierarchy. Use grouped bars or small multiples instead.

In a dense professional tool, typography discipline matters more than chart type: use tabular-figure (monospaced) number rendering in bar labels so columns align and scanning is fast. This is a common failure in SaaS cost dashboards that use proportional fonts in data labels.

scores.name: Cost Ledger / Pareto
scores.notes: Kills the callout bug structurally (donut demoted to optional label-free ring via hideCallouts; labels live in the ledger where they are already legible). A ranked horizontal-bar ledger is exactly how contractors read an estimate summary and is the research-endorsed default (Cleveland-McGill rank-1 position encoding vs donut rank 3-4). Reuses buckets/color/format untouched, already single-column so mobile is trivial. Lowest blast radius. Its one new fact (direct/misc/contingency composition) is gated behind a server payload change, and as written it risks ledger-bar vs BreakdownTable redundancy (the ledger MUST be the table). Data-richness is the weakest of the three because the cross-sheet insight engine stays dormant and there is no concentration/80% metric.

scores.name: Cost Anatomy
scores.notes: Boldest on the actual ask: leads with the never-shown direct/misc/contingency composition and frames contingency as first-class risk, then a ranked matrix. Kills the bug definitionally (no donut). Brand-clean. But the LEAD viz hard-depends on a server payload extension that does not exist yet, so Panel 1 cannot render at all until that ships - the single biggest build cost and a launch risk. The 3-segment strip can look near-solid on real sheets where misc/contingency are tiny (the common case), making the lead viz visually thin and forcing the insight line to carry it. Composition palette must sit outside Okabe-Ito yet stay AA. Feasibility is the gating weakness.

scores.name: Direction C - Insight-led / analyst
scores.notes: Best total. Answers the estimator's real question (biggest lever + single-group risk) in one plain-language sentence plus one scannable ranked ledger - it revives the already-built, already-in-production insight engine (used on the separate project-charts surface, dormant here). Kills the bug at the root (donut removed as lead). Crucially, the cross-sheet insight is feasible with ZERO repo change for the common <=20-sheet case because the Data repo already loads ALL sheets' series into seriesByEstimateId (all-estimates load mode); only >20 sheets needs the 1-line pair-load. Surfaces concentration (80% / groups-carrying-bulk) as pure client math - free, high-value, no payload change. Composition strip is its only server-gated piece and it is correctly scoped as a secondary strip, not the lead, so the page still ships fully if composition is deferred. Minor: needs a new single-sheet concentration sentence generator (sibling to the comparison one); auto-sentence edge cases (one bucket, equal, zero) must be handled; Category/Supplier drill needs a server child-aggregation so MVP drills Space-only.

judge.winner: Direction C - Insight-led / analyst Data page

recommendedSpec.thesis: Rebuild the Data page as a calm analyst's worksheet: a plain-language insight line plus the two or three numbers that matter lead each section, the primary breakdown is a single sorted horizontal-bar ledger read top-to-bottom (the donut is removed, not just demoted), and the page earns its keep by reviving the already-built-and-already-in-production insight engine for cross-sheet variance and by computing cost concentration client-side. The unreadable 720x560 donut callouts never render because the donut is gone from the lead; every label/amount/share/count lives inline on a positional bar that is readable at any width and degrades cleanly to one mobile column. New server data is limited to ONE optional, SEC-1-safe scalar triple (direct/misc/contingency) that powers a secondary strip the page can ship without.
